# Logos

Figma: [Logos](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-881)

The Safqah logo, in its 5 official color variants. Each variant is used for specific background conditions. The logo is a trademarked asset - never alter, redraw, or recreate it. Always use the supplied SVG files.

## Logo Variants

Five official color variants. Royal Green is the primary brand color and the default for most applications. Other variants exist for specific background conditions - light, dark, or branded surfaces where the primary green would clash or fail contrast.

## Clear Space

The Safqah logo requires a protected zone around it - equal to the height of the smallest mark (the diamond glyph). No other text, image, or graphic element should encroach inside this zone. This protects the logo from visual interference and maintains its presence.

The dashed outline represents the minimum clear space - equal to the height of the diamond glyph (X). No other elements should enter this zone.

## Minimum Sizes

Below these sizes the logo loses legibility and becomes visual noise. Always respect the floor. If a design needs a smaller mark, use a custom favicon or app icon instead - the wordmark cannot shrink below these limits.

Digital

24px tall

Minimum size for the full Safqah wordmark on screen.

Smaller than this, the wordmark letterforms break down. For favicons (16-32px) or app icons (smaller than 48px), use the diamond glyph only - not the full mark.

Print

8mm tall

Minimum size for the full Safqah wordmark in print.

On letterheads, business cards, and brochures, never go below 8mm. For embroidery, embossing, or other tactile reproductions, double this minimum to 16mm to preserve readability.

## Usage on Backgrounds

Pick the right variant based on the background it sits on. The goal is always visual presence with proper contrast. When a background falls into a gray zone, default to the Royal Green or the Dark variant - these read clearly on most surfaces.

| Background | Variant to use | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Off-White (Safqah's standard canvas) | Royal Green | Default brand expression. Warm cream gives the green its richest tone. |
| White or very light neutrals | Royal Green or Pigment Green | Royal Green for default. Pigment Green for high-energy contexts (campaign hero, video stings). |
| Dark / Black surfaces | Off-White | Best contrast on dark. Never use Royal Green on black - fails contrast and looks muddy. |
| Branded green surface (bg/brand/primary) | Off-White | Logo on its own primary background reads only in Off-White or White. |
| Yellow surface (bg/brand/yellow) | Dark | Yellow + brand green fails WCAG. Use Dark for sufficient contrast. |
| Photography (busy/varied) | Off-White with shadow, or Royal Green on a tinted panel | Test against the actual image. When in doubt, place the logo on a solid color block within the photo. |
| Print on uncoated paper | Royal Green or Dark | Yellow and Off-White don't reproduce well on uncoated stock. Stick with the two darker variants. |

## Misuse - Don't do this

The Safqah logo is a trademarked asset. The 5 official variants are the only permitted forms. The following alterations are prohibited.

| Don't Don't stretch, squash, or distort the logo. Always scale proportionally. | Don't Don't rotate, skew, or tilt the logo. The mark sits horizontally. | Don't Don't recolor the logo to a non-official color. Use only the 5 official variants. | Don't Don't apply effects (drop shadows, glows, bevels, outlines). The logo stands alone. | Don't Don't crop or partially obscure the logo. The full wordmark must be visible. | Don't Don't place the logo on busy patterns or low-contrast backgrounds without a solid panel. | Don't Don't recreate the logo from scratch or trace it. Always use the supplied SVG files. | Don't Don't modify the typography of the wordmark or add text adjacent to it without proper spacing. |

### Why the logo matters

A logo is the most condensed expression of a brand. For Safqah, the wordmark and diamond glyph together carry trust, professionalism, and the Saudi context of Sharia-compliant investment. Every time a user sees the mark - on a screen, in an email, on a contract - they're evaluating whether to trust their money with this brand. The logo is not decoration; it's a credential.

Design systems include logo guidelines for one reason: consistency builds trust. A logo that appears in different shades on different screens, or scaled wrong, or surrounded by competing graphics, tells users the company is loose with details. In financial services, looseness with details means looseness with money. The logo rules in this document are not aesthetic preferences - they're trust signals.

For Safqah operating in Saudi Arabia, the Royal Green carries cultural weight. Green is the color of safe & trust, of the Saudi national identity, and of growth. The shade chosen - a measured, professional green rather than a bright lime - communicates seriousness alongside the cultural resonance. Use it deliberately.

### The Safqah logo system

The system is intentionally small: one mark, five color variants, no alternative arrangements. This is by design - fewer choices mean fewer mistakes.

| Col 1 | Col 2 |
| --- | --- |
| One mark | The Safqah wordmark with the diamond glyph above. There is no stacked version, no horizontal-only variant, no monogram. The full mark is used everywhere the logo appears. For very small sizes where the wordmark would break down, use a custom app icon or favicon instead. |
| Five color variants | Royal Green (default), Pigment Green (high-energy), Yellow (accent on dark), Dark (monochrome on light), Off-White (inverse on dark). Each variant has a single official hex value. Don't introduce a sixth, even for "just this campaign." |
| SVG-first distribution | All variants are distributed as SVG. SVG scales infinitely, recolors via CSS in product UI, and ships small enough for any context. PNG exports are made for tools that can't consume SVG (Word, PowerPoint, some email clients). Always prefer SVG when possible. |

> **Tip:** Mental model: the logo is a constant. The variants exist only so the constant can appear on different backgrounds. The mark itself never changes - only its color shifts to suit context.

### Choosing the right variant

The variant choice is determined by background, not preference. Walk through this decision tree.

| Col 1 | Col 2 |
| --- | --- |
| Step 1 - Is the background dark (>50% black)? | Use Off-White. Royal Green doesn't have enough contrast on dark surfaces. Off-White is the only sanctioned light variant - never use pure white. |
| Step 2 - Is the background light and neutral (white, cream, light gray)? | Use Royal Green. This is the most common case - the default brand expression. |
| Step 3 - Is the background the brand green itself (bg/brand/primary)? | Use Off-White. Logo on its own primary color reads only in inverse. |
| Step 4 - Is the background brand yellow (bg/brand/yellow)? | Use Dark. Yellow + green fails contrast. Yellow + Off-White is too light. Dark gives the needed contrast. |
| Step 5 - Is the background a photograph or busy pattern? | Place the logo on a solid colored panel within the image (Off-White panel + Royal Green logo, or Dark panel + Off-White logo). Never place the logo directly on a busy image. |
| Step 6 - Is it print on uncoated stock? | Use Royal Green or Dark only. Yellow doesn't reproduce well on uncoated paper; it muddies. Off-White on uncoated stock disappears. |

> **Tip:** When uncertain between two valid variants, choose Royal Green. It's the default for a reason - it works in the widest range of contexts and most strongly communicates the Safqah identity.

### Working with partners and co-branding

When the Safqah logo appears alongside another brand's logo - for partnerships, sponsored content, or co-branded products - specific rules apply.

| Col 1 | Col 2 |
| --- | --- |
| Equal weight | Both logos should appear at the same optical size. If the partner mark is wider, scale Safqah to match its height. If taller, match its width. Never let Safqah dominate or shrink visually relative to a partner. |
| Separator | Use a vertical line, a plus sign (+), or generous whitespace to separate the marks. Never shove them directly together. The separator should be the same color as both marks (neutral text/default color works for most contexts). |
| Clear space applies to both | The Safqah clear-space rule applies to its presence in a lockup. The partner brand has its own clear-space rules that you must respect. The greater of the two distances is the actual separation needed. |
| Approval required | Co-branded materials must be approved by Safqah marketing before public release. The logo is a legal asset; misuse on partner channels reflects on the company. Always loop in brand leadership. |

> **Warning:** Never recreate, edit, or modify a partner's logo to match Safqah's style. The partner owns their mark and any modification is a trademark issue. Use the partner's supplied logo as-is.

### Anti-patterns (Don't do this)

Common mistakes when working with the logo. These are repeated industry pitfalls - avoid them.

> **Don't:** Don't download the logo from a Google search, screenshot, or third-party site. Logos from these sources are often outdated, low-resolution, or unofficial variants. Always use the SVG files supplied through this design system.

> **Don't:** Don't change the logo color to match a campaign theme. The 5 variants are the only sanctioned colors. If a campaign needs a brand mark that fits a different palette, the answer is the Off-White or Dark variant, not a new color.

> **Don't:** Don't place the logo inside a colored box that becomes a "logo container." The logo stands on its own. Containers fragment brand presence across applications.

> **Don't:** Don't scale the logo to under 24px (digital) or 8mm (print). Below those sizes, the wordmark letterforms break down and the logo becomes visual noise rather than a brand signal.

> **Don't:** Don't add taglines, slogans, or sub-brand text directly attached to the logo. Taglines belong as separate typography below or beside the logo, with full clear-space respected.

> **Don't:** Don't animate, distort, or "creatively interpret" the logo for video, social posts, or interactive content without explicit approval from Safqah marketing. The mark sits still.

> **Don't:** Don't convert the SVG paths to a font or icon font. Logos in icon fonts get reused inappropriately and lose color fidelity. Always treat the logo as the supplied SVG, not as a typographic glyph.
